# Hostile input fixtures

Tiny, hand-crafted malformed PDFs, kept as regression inputs for the crash
bugs a review round found in the readers. They contain no certificate
material, no signature and nothing that ever came out of a real signer:
every byte is synthetic and every file is a few hundred bytes long.

- `sig-contents-short.pdf` — a `/Type /Sig` dictionary whose `/Contents` is
  `<3084>`: a DER long-form length that claims four length octets in a value
  of two bytes. Reading the contents used to slice past the end and panic.
- `xref-at-eof.pdf` — a document whose `startxref` points into the last
  `%%EOF` line, so the object header scan runs off the end of the file. The
  error *message* for that case used to slice eight bytes past the end and
  panic before it could be returned.
- `xref-entries-bomb.pdf` — an 86 KB document whose cross-reference stream
  declares `/Size 30000000` with `/W [1 1 1]`: a ~90 MB row table behind a
  file smaller than a page. Before the entry cap it died by allocation
  inside `Vec::with_capacity`, so no error could even be returned; now the
  walk refuses the claim by name before materialising anything.

The tests that use them live in `crates/openfirma-pades/tests/hostile.rs`,
which also builds further hostile documents (impossible `/ByteRange`
numbers, truncated cross-reference tables) in memory instead of as files.

## Wave-3 protocol bait (regenerated by `tools/gen-hostile-corpus.py`)

DER — every length-cursor entry point shares them (`cades::verify`, the TSP
readers, CRL/OCSP parsing, PKCS#12):

- `der-contentinfo-trunc.der` (4 B) — `30 82 01`: a long-form length that
  promises two following octets and carries one. The cursor bug of wave 3:
  slicing the length bytes without checking they are all there.
- `der-longlen-huge.der` (12 B) — `30 89 FF…FF 00`: a nine-octet length,
  2^64−1 of content in a twelve byte file; must refuse before any allocation.
- `der-seq-eol.der` (5 B) — `30 05 02 01 FF`: a SEQUENCE claiming five payload
  bytes from three. Children may not cross the end of their parent, and the
  parent may not cross the end of the file.
- `der-null-len.der` (2 B) — `30 80`: BER indefinite length, which DER (and
  every entry point here) refuses outright.

XML — fed to `xml::parse` and, on success, straight into `c14n::document`:

- `xml-truncated-tag.xml` (64 B) — an element cut mid-attribute; the EOF
  family that used to slice past the end of the source.
- `xml-undeclared-prefix.xml` (56 B) — prefixes with no binding anywhere in
  scope: canonicalization must produce bytes or a clean error, never a panic
  over an empty axis (the wave-3 Scope rewrite's target shape).
- `xml-deep-nesting.xml` (981 B) — 140 nested `<a>` elements: deep but inside
  the parser's MAX_DEPTH (512), so it must *parse*; hostile depth beyond the
  limit is refused by name and covered in xades' own suite.
- `xml-bad-utf8.xml` (16 B) — non-UTF-8 bytes where text content sits.

PKCS#12 — both are DER-shaped headers over too little file:

- `p12-garbage-head.p12` (36 B) — a PFX header (`30 82 01 66`) followed by
  forty bytes of SHA-256-seeded junk: structure past the header is garbage.
- `p12-truncated-header.p12` (2 B) — the same header cut after two bytes:
  wave 3's M1 family, a container that promises 358 bytes and has none.

The tests that execute all of this (plus a deterministic single-byte mutation
sweep over the golden specimens) live in
`crates/openfirma-cli/tests/hostile_corpus.rs`; they run on every `cargo test`
and therefore on every CI job — finding H-11's cheap half. The PDF fixtures
above remain owned by `crates/openfirma-pades/tests/hostile.rs`.
